Ticket Id: 16074

10/04/2010

Dr B Townsend

Emergency department

Newtown Children's Hospital

Dear Dr Townsend,

Re: Emma Johnson, aged 11 years old

I am writing this letter to refer you Emma Johnson, an 11-year-old child, whose features are consistent
with severe asthma which was triggered by a viral upper respiratory infection. Your urgent assessment
would be highly appreciated.

Regarding her family history, she has a family history of asthma, which affected both her mother and her
older sister.

Upon first visit, the patient attended my surgery complaining of nocturnal cough associated with mild fever   Commented [JG1]: the
and runny nose. On examination, her PEFR was 250 L/min.Thus, she was given Paracetamol and fluids.            Commented [JG2]: paracetamol
Three weeks later, she returned with a persistent nocturnal cough. On examination, her chest showed a
basal wheezes and her PFER declined more to reach 230 L/min. Therefore, she was commenced on Trail            Commented [JG3]: a trial of
inhaled salbutamol. Moreover, in the next two visits, her symptoms gradually improved and her PFER            Commented [JG4]: on
surged to 340 L/min. Thus, she was commenced on inhaled corticosteroid.

Today, she complained of a worsening shortness of breath and a 48 hours duration of widespread wheezes
associated with fever, runny nose and lost of appetite. Upon examination, there was a red throat and          Commented [JG5]: loss
obvious breathing difficulty as she used her accessory muscles. Furthermore, her PFER plummeted to 140
L/min.

In light of the above, your management and assessment is required promptly. If you have any queries,          Commented [JG6]: are
please do not hesitate to contact me.

Yours sincerely,

Doctor
